memory_candidates: CSLib Propositional Intuitionistic tableau: F-and and T-or are BETA (branching) rules; F-or and T-and are ALPHA (non-branching) rules. This means a single tableau branch can accumulate multiple sibling worlds at the same creation-depth whenever F-imp obligations are combined via alpha-decomposable or/and connectives -- a naive ancestor-chain-depth argument is insufficient to bound total world count on one branch; an occurrence-tracking argument over the monotonically-growing `expanded` set is needed instead.

When a Lean file imports another file for a lemma used only inside a proof body (e.g. Cslib.Foundations.Logic.Tableau.Measure for sum_map_le_length_mul), also check whether that imported file's OWN tactic imports (e.g. Mathlib.Tactic.Ring) are private (plain `import`, not `public import`) -- if so, the tactic will not be transitively available and must be imported directly in the new file too.
